fact_text: Price to book (P/B) divides a stock's market price by its book value per share, showing how many rupees of market price investors pay for each rupee of book value.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'STOP Overpaying for Stocks in PSX with This One Ratio! Book Value And P/B Ratio | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-13)

fact_text: Book value is what remains after a company's liabilities are deducted from its assets, which is the owners' equity shown on the balance sheet.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'STOP Overpaying for Stocks in PSX with This One Ratio! Book Value And P/B Ratio | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-13)

fact_text: Book value per share is total book value divided by the number of shares outstanding, and both inputs are found in the company's balance sheet and share data.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'STOP Overpaying for Stocks in PSX with This One Ratio! Book Value And P/B Ratio | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-13)

fact_text: A P/B ratio of 1 means the market price equals book value, a ratio below 1 means the stock trades under book value, and a ratio above 1 means a premium to book.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'STOP Overpaying for Stocks in PSX with This One Ratio! Book Value And P/B Ratio | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-13)

fact_text: Equity grows over time through retained earnings, the share of profit a company keeps in the business for growth rather than paying out as dividends.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'STOP Overpaying for Stocks in PSX with This One Ratio! Book Value And P/B Ratio | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-13)

fact_text: Book value matters most for capital-intensive companies whose operations rest on plant, property and equipment, and it is less useful for service and technology firms.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'STOP Overpaying for Stocks in PSX with This One Ratio! Book Value And P/B Ratio | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-13)

fact_text: The analyst warns that P/B is only one parameter, so it should be combined with other ratios before an investment decision is taken.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'STOP Overpaying for Stocks in PSX with This One Ratio! Book Value And P/B Ratio | Afaque Manzar |' (YouTube, 2024-11-13)
